proposals.before: Zong Chuke, Wu Sansi, Wu Yanxiu, and their allies were then taking turns as court factions. Riyong quietly attached himself to each in turn and was rapidly promoted to Vice Minister of War and concurrently a Xiuxian Hall academician.
proposals.after: Zong Chuke, Wu Sansi, Wu Yanxiu, and their allies were then taking turns as court factions. Riyong quietly attached himself to each in turn and was rapidly promoted to Vice Minister of War and concurrently a Xiuwen Hall academician.
proposals.reason: 修文館 is Xiuwen, not Xiuxian; the hall name is mistransliterated.

proposals.before: Learning that Prince Lin (the future Xuanzong) was planning a coup, he used the monk Purun and the Daoist Wang Ye as intermediaries to visit the prince's residence in secret, pledged himself deeply, and plotted to help place him on the throne.
proposals.after: Learning that Xuanzong was planning a righteous rising, he used the monk Purun and the Daoist Wang Ye as intermediaries to visit the princely residence in secret, pledged himself deeply, and plotted to support and elevate him.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names 玄宗, not Prince Lin; the parenthetical identity is an interpretive insertion.

proposals.before: He was soon sent out as Senior Administrator of Yangzhou, then served in turn as prefect of Wu and Bian, Military Commissioner of Yanzhou, and Senior Administrator of Jingzhou.
proposals.after: He was soon sent out as Senior Administrator of Yangzhou, then served in turn as prefect of Wuzhou and Bianzhou, Military Commissioner of Yanzhou, and Senior Administrator of Jingzhou.
proposals.reason: 婺 is Wuzhou, not the bare name Wu; Bian should likewise be Bianzhou.

proposals.before: At twenty he took the Five Classics examination, was appointed magistrate of Pingxiang, but was dismissed for an offense and returned home.
proposals.after: At twenty he took the Five Classics examination, was appointed commandant of Pingxiang, but was dismissed for an offense and returned home.
proposals.reason: Pingxiang wei is a county commandant, not a magistrate.

proposals.before: My younger brother Jiayou has just been appointed Vice Prefect of Binzhou; we are posted to opposite ends of the empire, united in heart yet separated in body, our spirits torn apart by ten thousand li.
proposals.after: My younger brother Jiayou has just been appointed Vice Prefect of Shanzhou; we are posted to opposite ends of the empire, united in heart yet separated in body, our spirits torn apart by ten thousand li.
proposals.reason: Chinese toponym is Shanzhou, not Binzhou.

proposals.before: My younger brother Jiayou is now appointed Vice Prefect of Bin; he and I are each in a different region—of one heart yet dwelling apart, our spirits severed by ten thousand li.
proposals.after: My younger brother Jiayou is now appointed Vice Prefect of Shan; he and I are each in a different region—of one heart yet dwelling apart, our spirits severed by ten thousand li.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise renders Shanzhou as Bin.

proposals.before: Soon afterward Military Commissioner of Guangzhou Pei Xianxian was imprisoned; the Emperor asked his ministers what sentence was appropriate, and Jiazhen again petitioned for corporal punishment.
proposals.after: Soon afterward Military Commissioner of Guangzhou Pei Zhouxian was imprisoned; the Emperor asked his ministers what sentence was appropriate, and Jiazhen again petitioned for corporal punishment.
proposals.reason: Chinese 裴伷先 is Pei Zhouxian (伷), not Xianxian.

proposals.before: Pei should be exiled according to the facts of his case; he must not be beaten again on a whim."
proposals.after: Zhouxian should be exiled according to the facts of his case; he must not be beaten again on a whim."
proposals.reason: The shortened English Pei continues the mistranslation of 伷先; the Chinese names Pei Zhouxian.

proposals.before: Zhang Yue urged Jiazhen to wear mourning dress and await judgment, barring him from court audience; Jiazhen was sent out as prefect of Youzhou, and Yue replaced him as Director of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: Zhang Yue urged Jiazhen to wear plain dress and await judgment, barring him from court audience; Jiazhen was sent out as prefect of Youzhou, and Yue replaced him as Director of the Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 素服待罪 is plain clothing while awaiting punishment, not mourning dress.

proposals.before: The Emperor was moved as well and immediately summoned the youth, bestowing the name Yanbao and specially appointing him Military Staff Officer of the Left Inner Rate.
proposals.after: The Emperor was moved as well and immediately summoned the youth, bestowing the name Yanshang and specially appointing him Military Staff Officer of the Left Inner Rate.
proposals.reason: 延賞 is Yanshang, not Yanbao.

proposals.before: Since the Kaiyuan reign more than ten Xiangzhou prefects had died or been demoted in office. Jiayou learned that Yuwen Jiong had served as area commander of Xiang at the end of the Northern Zhou and died for the state, and he established a shrine to Jiong's spirit to seek divine protection.
proposals.after: Since the Kaiyuan reign more than ten Xiangzhou prefects had died or been demoted in office. Jiayou learned that Yuchi Jiong had served as area commander of Xiang at the end of the Northern Zhou and died for the state, and he established a shrine to Jiong's spirit to seek divine protection.
proposals.reason: Chinese 尉遲迥 is the surname Yuchi, not Yuwen.

proposals.before: Later, when Wu Jing became prefect of Ye, he added imperial regalia to Yuwen's spirit image as well.
proposals.after: Later, when Wu Jing became prefect of Ye, he added imperial regalia to Yuchi's spirit image as well.
proposals.reason: The English continues the Yuwen misreading of 尉遲.

proposals.before: Xiao Song was the great-grandnephew of Xiao Yu, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and Duke of Song in early Zhenguan.
proposals.after: Xiao Song was the great-grandnephew of Xiao Yu, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Duke of Song in early Zhenguan.
proposals.reason: 左僕射 is the Left Pushe of Shangshu, not of the Secretariat.

proposals.before: When Han Xiu became chief minister he was stern and upright and would not defer to Song; they argued before the Emperor until Song offered to resign.
proposals.after: When Han Xiu became chief minister, Song raised affairs; Xiu was stern and upright and would not defer to him; they argued before the Emperor until Song offered to resign.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 嵩舉事 is omitted in the idiomatic English, which jumps from Han Xiu's appointment to his sternness and thereby drops Song's initiation of business as the trigger of the clash.

proposals.before: The following autumn Tibet invaded in force; Ximoming again led troops against Guazhou, but Shougui drove them off.
proposals.after: The following autumn Tibet invaded in force; Ximoming then led troops against Guazhou, but Shougui drove them off.
proposals.reason: 復 here continues the Tibetan offensive; Ximoming has not previously appeared leading an attack, so English 'again' invents a prior Ximoming campaign.

proposals.before: Xiao Hua, Song's son Hua, at the end of Tianbao was transferred to Vice Minister of War.
proposals.after: Xiao Hua, at the end of Tianbao, was transferred to Vice Minister of War.
proposals.reason: The sentence 蕭華子華 names Xiao Hua; it does not mention Song. The literal line invents 'Song's son Hua'.

proposals.before: After the rout at Xiangzhou Hua returned to the capital but, still tainted by his service under the rebels, was demoted to provisional Vice Director of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: After the rout at Xiangzhou, Hua returned to the capital but, still tainted by his service under the rebels, was demoted to provisional Vice Director of the Secretariat.
proposals.reason: A comma is required after Xiangzhou; without it English fuses the place with Hua as a single name.

proposals.before: Hua's sons were Heng and Wu.
proposals.after: Hua's sons were Chang and Wu.
proposals.reason: 恆 is a different person from 衡 (Xiao Heng). Rendering 恆 as Heng, the same English as 衡, fuses two brothers' lines.

proposals.before: Heng's son Fu became chief minister in the Dahe era (827–835).
proposals.after: Chang's son Fu became chief minister in the Dahe era (827–835).
proposals.reason: 恆子俯 is the son of Hua's son 恆, not Xiao Heng 衡 or Heng's son 復 already named in s0207.

proposals.before: The Emperor replied, "Do not, like Wang Yifu who recognized Shi Le too late, mistakenly harm a loyal man."
proposals.after: The Emperor replied, "Do not use the anecdote of Wang Yifu recognizing Shi Le and thereby mistakenly harm a loyal man."
proposals.reason: The Chinese 王夷甫知石勒故事 names a known historical anecdote, not a claim that Wang recognized Shi Le 'too late'.

proposals.before: He soon requested leave to visit his parents' tombs, fell ill on the journey, and died at sixty-eight. He was posthumously made Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhou and given the posthumous title Wenxian ("Literary Exemplar").
proposals.after: He soon requested leave to visit the tombs, then fell ill and died, aged sixty-eight; he was posthumously made Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhou, with the posthumous title Wenxian.
proposals.reason: 拜墓 does not specify parents in the plural; the idiomatic English invents 'his parents' tombs' and 'on the journey'.

proposals.before: E Prefect Cui Fa insulted a junior eunuch attendant, provoking Emperor Jingzong's fierce anger; he was handed over to the censorate for investigation.
proposals.after: Magistrate Cui Fa of Hu County insulted a junior eunuch attendant, provoking Emperor Jingzong's fierce anger; he was handed over to the censorate for investigation.
proposals.reason: 鄠縣令 is magistrate of Hu County, not ‘E Prefect’; 鄠 is Hu.

proposals.before: In 835, as Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, when ministers and generals connected to the Sweet Dew incident were slaughtered en masse, Zhongfang secretly ordered their bodies identified.
proposals.after: In the ninth year of Dahe, as Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, when ministers and generals who had been implicated were slaughtered en masse, Zhongfang secretly ordered their bodies identified.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 將相從累者 does not name the Sweet Dew Incident; that historical identification is invented in the idiomatic English.

proposals.before: Soldiers were running rampant at the time, and Zhongfang was regarded as too mild and ineffectual for the crisis. He was found unfit for office, appointed governor of Hua Prefecture, and later transferred to be Director of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: Soldiers were running rampant at the time, and Zhongfang was regarded as too mild and ineffectual for the crisis. He was found unfit for office, appointed governor of Hua Prefecture, and later transferred to be Director of the Palace Library.
proposals.reason: 秘書監 is Director of the Palace Library, not Director of the Secretariat (中書).

proposals.before: Li Shizhi—Li Shizhi, also named Chang, was a grandson of Prince of Hengshan Chengqian.
proposals.after: Li Shizhi, also named Chang, was a grandson of Prince of Hengshan Chengqian.
proposals.reason: The literal line repeats ‘Li Shizhi’ after the em dash without a source basis.

proposals.before: When Han Chaozong of the Secretariat was serving as an inspection commissioner, he singled Shizhi out in a memorial of recommendation, and Shizhi was promoted to Area Commander of Qin Prefecture.
proposals.after: When Supervising Secretary Han Chaozong was serving as an inspection commissioner, he singled Shizhi out in a memorial of recommendation, and Shizhi was promoted to Area Commander of Qin Prefecture.
proposals.reason: 給事中 is Supervising Secretary, not ‘of the Secretariat’ in this phrasing.

proposals.before: Li Jiqing, styled Zi Jiqing, passed the Mingjing examination in his youth and showed considerable talent for literary composition.
proposals.after: His son Li Jiqing passed the Mingjing examination in his youth and showed considerable talent for literary composition.
proposals.reason: Chinese 子 marks filiation after Li Shizhi's biography, not a courtesy name Zi Jiqing.

proposals.before: Li Jiqing—Zi Jiqing—at the age of weak cap passed the Mingjing examination and was quite skilled in literary composition.
proposals.after: His son Li Jiqing, at the age of weak cap, passed the Mingjing examination and was quite skilled in literary composition.
proposals.reason: The literal likewise treats 子 as a style name; it is the kinship term son.

proposals.before: Li Rong, styled Sun Rong, was upright and disciplined by nature and skilled in administrative affairs.
proposals.after: His grandson Li Rong was upright and disciplined by nature and skilled in administrative affairs.
proposals.reason: Chinese 孫 marks him as grandson, not a courtesy name Sun Rong.

proposals.before: Li Rong—Sun Rong—had a nature upright and strict and was skilled in administrative affairs.
proposals.after: His grandson Li Rong had a nature upright and strict and was skilled in administrative affairs.
proposals.reason: The literal likewise treats 孫 as a style name rather than grandson.

proposals.before: His uncle Fangyan served as a director in the Ministry of Revenue during the Jingyun era.
proposals.after: His uncle Fang Ni served as a director in the Ministry of Revenue during the Jingyun era.
proposals.reason: 方嶷 is Fang Ni; Fangyan misreads 嶷.

proposals.before: His uncle Fangyan, in the Jingyun period, was Langzhong in the Ministry of Revenue.
proposals.after: His uncle Fang Ni, in the Jingyun period, was Langzhong in the Ministry of Revenue.
proposals.reason: Same misreading of 嶷 in the literal English.

proposals.before: He took the special imperial examination and passed in Broad Learning and Eloquent Composition, then rose twice to the post of county magistrate of Hu in the Jingzhao metropolitan prefecture.
proposals.after: He took the special imperial examination and passed in Broad Learning and Eloquent Composition, then rose twice to the post of county defender (wei) of Hu in the Jingzhao metropolitan prefecture.
proposals.reason: 鄠縣尉 is county wei, not magistrate.

proposals.before: Wang Maoqi of the Palace Domestic Service had been sent to Taiyuan, Shuofang, and You to audit troops and horses. Years passed, and he then sent an official dispatch to Taiyuan demanding arms and equipment.
proposals.after: Wang Maozhong, Director of the Palace Administration, had been sent to Taiyuan, Shuofang, and You to audit troops and horses. Years passed, and he then sent an official dispatch to Taiyuan demanding arms and equipment.
proposals.reason: 王毛仲 is Wang Maozhong (仲 = zhòng), not Maoqi; 殿中監 is the Director of the Palace Administration, not the Palace Domestic Service.

proposals.before: In the twentieth year Wang Maoqi fell from favor and was ordered to die. Xuanzong remembered Tingzhi's earlier memorial, promoted him to Vice Minister of Justice, and showed him deep favor before appointing him Director of the Grand Treasury.
proposals.after: In the twentieth year of Kaiyuan, Wang Maozhong fell from favor and was ordered to die. Xuanzong remembered Tingzhi's earlier memorial, promoted him to Vice Minister of Justice, and showed him deep favor before appointing him Director of the Grand Treasury.
proposals.reason: The inherited reign is Kaiyuan, so 二十年 is Kaiyuan 20; 王毛仲 should be Wang Maozhong, matching 仲.

proposals.before: At that time Pei Yaojing as Palace Attendant, Li Linfu as Minister of Rites, and Zhang Jiuling all served together as chancellors. Jiuling had risen through literary talent, reviewed drafts in the Hanlin Academy, and also served as Director of the Secretariat, enjoying exceptional favor from the throne.
proposals.after: At that time Pei Yaoqing as Palace Attendant, Li Linfu as Minister of Rites, and Zhang Jiuling all served together as chancellors. Jiuling had risen through literary talent, reviewed drafts in the Hanlin Academy, and also served as Director of the Secretariat, enjoying exceptional favor from the throne.
proposals.reason: 裴耀卿 is Pei Yaoqing (卿 = qīng), not Yaojing.

proposals.before: Li Linfu then summoned Tingzhi's younger brother Sunzhi to his house to renew old acquaintance, promising that Sunzhi's son would be given an outside post. He told Sunzhi, "His Majesty thinks very highly of your elder brother. You must find a way for him to enter the capital for an audience—he will surely be given a major appointment."
proposals.after: Li Linfu then summoned Tingzhi's younger brother Sunzhi to his house to renew old acquaintance, promising that Sunzhi's son would be appointed a Vice Director (Yuanwailang). He told Sunzhi, "His Majesty thinks very highly of your elder brother. You must find a way for him to enter the capital for an audience—he will surely be given a major appointment."
proposals.reason: 員外郎 is the specific office Yuanwailang, not a generic outside post.

proposals.before: Although Zhang Jiazhen did not establish estates, alas he was eager for power and profit, formed factions with those near him, and had Jiang Jiao and Xianxian beaten with the staff—he was not a man of impartial standing.
proposals.after: Although Zhang Jiazhen did not establish estates, alas he was eager for power and profit, formed factions with those near him, and had Jiang Jiao and Pei Xianxian beaten with the staff—he was not a man of impartial standing.
proposals.reason: Literal English drops the surname already supplied for 伷先 in the idiomatic line (Pei Xianxian), leaving a bare given name that obscures the referent.

proposals.before: Song, Ling, Shizhi, and Ting each had his measure and standard.
proposals.after: Song, Jiuling, Shizhi, and Ting each had his measure and standard.
proposals.reason: 齡 here continues 九齡 from the preceding appraisal; rendering it as Ling rather than Jiuling breaks the same-person reference the idiomatic line already keeps.

decisions.reason: 修文館 is Xiuwen Hall; Xiuxian misreads 文 as 仙.
The unit names 玄宗 and 義舉; Prince Lin and 'coup' are not in the Chinese.
婺州 and 汴州 are Wuzhou and Bianzhou; bare Wu invites confusion with 吳.
平鄉尉 is a county commandant (尉), not a magistrate (令).
鄯州 is Shanzhou; Binzhou would be 邠州.
The same 鄯州 error appears in the literal English as Bin.
伷 is Zhou, so 裴伷先 is Pei Zhouxian, not Xianxian.
This sentence names him 伷先; English Pei uses the already established surname 裴 and is accurate enough. Switching to the given name is optional style.
素服待罪 is plain dress while awaiting punishment, not mourning clothes.
延賞 is Yanshang; Yanbao would require 寶.
尉遲 is the surname Yuchi; Yuwen is 宇文.

decisions.reason: 尉遲神 continues the same surname Yuchi, not Yuwen.
左僕射 is the Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs (尚書), not of the Secretariat.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 貞觀初左僕射、宋國公瑀

decisions.after: When Han Xiu became chief minister, Song took the initiative in handling business; Xiu was stern and upright and would not defer to him; they argued before the Emperor until Song offered to resign.
decisions.reason: 嵩舉事 is omitted in the original, a real gap, but 'Song raised affairs' is awkward English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 及休入相，嵩舉事，休峭直

decisions.reason: In the supplied window 悉末明 has not previously attacked; 復 here is sequential 'then', not a second Ximoming campaign.
蕭華子華 names Xiao Hua; Song is not in this sentence, so 'Song's son Hua' is an insertion.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 蕭華子華，天寶末轉兵部侍郎

decisions.reason: After the rout at Xiangzhou Hua returned is ordinary English (place + subject); the comma is stylistic, not a fused name.
恆 is Hua's son, distinct from 衡 in the previous sentence; rendering both as Heng fuses two men. Chang keeps them apart in English.
恆子俯 is the son of Hua's son 恆, not 衡's son 復 of s0207.
王夷甫知石勒故事 cites that anecdote; it does not say Wang recognized Shi Le too late.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 卿勿以王夷甫知石勒故事，誤害忠良

decisions.after: He soon requested leave to return and pay respects at the graves, then fell ill and died at sixty-eight. He was posthumously made Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhou and given the posthumous title Wenxian ("Literary Exemplar").
decisions.reason: 歸拜墓 does not say parents, and 因遇疾卒 does not say he fell ill on the journey; those are real inventions. The proposed line is still abrupt and drops the useful Wenxian gloss.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 俄請歸拜墓，因遇疾卒，年六十八

decisions.reason: 鄠縣令 is magistrate of Hu County, not E Prefect.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 時鄠縣令崔發因辱小黃門

decisions.reason: 將相從累者 are implicated ministers and generals; the Sweet Dew name is not in the Chinese.
秘書監 is Director of the Palace Library, not of the Secretariat.
李適之 appears once; the repeated 'Li Shizhi—' has no source.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 李適之，一名昌，恆山王承乾之孫也

decisions.reason: 給事中 is Supervising Secretary of the Chancellery, not an official 'of the Secretariat'.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 時給事中韓朝宗為按察使

decisions.reason: After Shizhi's death, 子 marks Li Jiqing as his son; it is not a courtesy name Zi Jiqing.
The literal likewise misreads kinship 子 as a style name.
孫 marks Li Rong as grandson, not a courtesy name Sun Rong.
The literal likewise misreads kinship 孫 as a style name.
方嶷 is Fang Ni; Fangyan misreads 嶷.
The literal has the same misreading of 嶷.

decisions.after: He took the special imperial examination and passed in Broad Learning and Eloquent Composition, then rose twice to the post of commandant of Hu County in the Jingzhao metropolitan prefecture.
decisions.reason: 鄠縣尉 is a county commandant, not a magistrate, but 'county defender (wei)' is awkward beside commandant used for 尉 elsewhere.
王毛仲 is Wang Maozhong; 殿中監 is Director of the Palace Administration, not the Palace Domestic Service.
二十年 in this Kaiyuan narrative is Kaiyuan 20, and 毛仲 is Maozhong, not Maoqi.
裴耀卿 is Pei Yaoqing; Yaojing misreads 卿.
當授子員外郎 promises the office of yuanwailang, not a generic outside post.

decisions.after: Although Zhang Jiazhen did not establish estates, alas he was eager for power and profit, formed factions with those near him, and had Jiang Jiao and Pei Zhouxian beaten with the staff—he was not a man of impartial standing.
decisions.reason: Adding the surname 裴 is right, but 伷先 is Zhouxian, so Pei Xianxian repeats the given-name error.
齡 in 嵩、齡、適、挺 continues 九齡 from the preceding appraisal, i.e. Jiuling, not a separate Ling.
